full_judgment:
"Section 30 seems to be based on the view that an admission by an accused person of his own guilt affords some sort of sanction in support of the truth of his confession against others as well as himself. But a confession of a co-accused is obviously evidence of a very weak type. It does not indeed come within the definition of "evidence" contained in section 3, Evidence Act. It is not required to be given on oath, nor in the presence of the accused, and it cannot be tested by cross-examination. It is a much weaker type of evidence than the evidence of an approver which is not subject to any of those infirmities. Section 30, however, provides that the court may take the confession into consideration and thereby, no doubt, makes it evidence on which the Court may act; but the section does not say that the confession is to amount to proof. Clearly there must be other evidence. The confession is only one element in the consideration of all the facts proved in the case, it can be put into the scale and weighed with the other evidence. Their Lordships think that the view which has prevailed in most of the High Courts in India, namely, that the confession of a co-accused can be used only in support of other evidence and cannot be made the foundation of conviction, is correct." 

 194. The evidence that Major Aziz Pasha with the sten gun of Risalder Moslemuddin fired stengun shots on Begum Mujib and on the inmates of the room is not at variance with the statement made under section 161 Code of Criminal Procedure before the Investigating officer as PW 61 saying that Major Aziz Pasha fired shot on all inside the room with the stengun of Risalder Moslemuddin. The purpose of bringing in the previous statement is to confront the maker for the purpose of contradicting him and if contradicted to discredit him, the credence of PW 4 may be impeached by proof of former statement before the Investigating Officer inconsistent with any part of his evidence, which is liable to be contradicted. 

 222. PW 47 is Major General (Retd) Khalilur Rahman, who has stated that he was the BDR Chief at the material time and while his wife saying morning prayer heard the sound of firing and at this woke him up and asked it seems that there is firing, look what is happening. He then and there telephoned the duty officer of BDR who also confirmed of the sounds of firing. This witness instructed to take information sending a man. Thereafter making the radio on, heard the sound of Major Dalim who is giving declaration that "Sheikh Mujib has peen killed." Hearing the same he instructed the duty officer to set one wing ready for action. Then he went to the office being ready and asked the senior Office for discussion. While discusing about the situation at about  9-00 AM, heard the declaration of allegiance by three Chiefs of Staff. Hearing the same they have changed course of discussion. At about 9-30 AM some army captain sought his interview who came with a message from Major Rashed and Major Farook that 'what we the juniors did you seniors shall take the burden and save the country. Other senior officers are at the radio station, you come sharp after discussion all the work will be done accordingly? After seeing off the captain he had talk with the BDR Sector Commanders in different Border areas and upon discussion everybody was unanimous that as all the three chiefs of staff had owed allegiance to the changed government, at this situation any step by BDR would amount to civil war. After this decision he communicated to all the BDR Sector Commanders at the border who agreed with him. Meanwhile there were 2/3 telephone calls from radio office asking him to go there. At about 10-30-11-00 AM he went to the radio office where he was taken in a room and saw Khondaker Mostaque and Taheruddin Thakur. In the midst of their conversation Major Dalim also came there. Khondaker Mostaque told him whatever has happened you tackle the situation and save the country. This witness replied 'all right that will be done'. Then a written paper was handed over to him which he read over and the same was recorded. Thereafter they were taken to Bangabhaban where two ceremonies of oath taking took place one of President and another of Council of Ministers. Apart from the 3 chiefs of staffs, Major Rashed, Major Farook, Major Noor, Major Shahriar, Major Dalim, Major Bazlul Huda, Major Aziz Pasha, Major Mohiuddin (Lancer) Risaldar Moslemuddin were seen present. 

 267. The fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence is that the accused is presumed to be innocent unless contrary is proved. Thus the contrary proof is the heavy burden upon the prosecution to rebut the presumption leading cogent evidence as to the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. 

 268. The theory of proof of the guilt beyond reasonable doubt varies from case to case in the facts and circumstances of the case. Law does not require a particular number of witnesses to prove a case and conviction may be based on the sole testimony of a witness.
